column1: # The one record of what actually ran in a host. Every prose claim about a host
# has to agree with a row here; `tools/check-docs.py` reads this file and fails a
# document that says a host with a row has never run something.

column7: default gain; mae 0.0 and max 0 over 8294400 bytes, so the frame is the source to the byte (the .log beside it prints only the frame size)
gain 2.0; mae 0.0 and max 0 against the doubled source; 1920x1080 PNG is the source times two to the byte, so render() ran
mae 0.0 over 8294400 bytes; the declaration names the CUDA path for all eight invocations
host killed with a job in flight; the run ends fail with the host exit code in 47 s
tier 3 of verify-bundle.bat with the GPU processing mode on Auto; the host logs "Compute API set to automatic, defaulting to CUDA", the effect is applied and one 1920x1080 frame decodes
the same tier with the mode set to CUDA; the log carries "Selected compute API: CUDA" and no automatic line, and the preference was restored afterwards
one 256x256 frame through testkit/verify-bundle.bat, pixels checked

the host hands over no OpenCL queue: nine render() calls arrive with opencl=0 and a null pOpenCLCmdQ (eight 1920x1080 frames and one 208x117 preview window), and the frame is the source times 2.0 to the byte; the host is in CUDA mode, so it offers CUDA buffers, not an OpenCL queue

describe() accepts every write the template makes except kOfxImageEffectPropCPURenderSupported; with that one guarded, the host instantiates the effect, creates the filter context and renders 1920x1080 with the model's output - mae 94.87 against the source, and mae 0.198 of 255 (max 0.5) against the same model run on the CPU (onnx-describe-resolve.log)

the provider-only bundle on the clean CUDA-12 pairing - ONNX Runtime 1.20.1, four files and no CUDA runtime of its own, from a clean build directory: the host logs "Selected compute API: CUDA", renders 1920x1080, and $ONNX_PROVIDER_LOG reads "CUDA (device 0, 1 thread, bundled CUDA, tf32 off, arena kSameAsRequested, all nodes on CUDA)"; run twice that day, 18:49 and 19:10 after the rebuild, same label. The 2026-11-26 sessions of the same bundle never instantiated: describe() threw on kOfxImageEffectPropCPURenderSupported (onnx-describe-resolve.log)

the 1.32.0 provider-only bundle, imports cuBLAS 13 and gated at major 13: the host logs CUDA, renders 1920x1080 and the label reads all nodes on CUDA - because CUDA 13.0 is on PATH on this machine, so this is a contaminated environment, not Resolve supplying CUDA 13

the imported-project route, closed: a .drp this host exported is brought back with ImportProject -> True, opened by its base name with LoadProject, and renders 1920x1080 Complete in 808 ms with mae 94.873 against the source and $ONNX_PROVIDER_LOG reading CUDA, all nodes on CUDA, model from Contents/Resources/model.onnx. Host started with --gui: -nogui reached no scriptable host in four attempts that hour. The same route on the pre-guard bundle produced a source-identical frame and dozens of 'Create context ... failed' lines (row19-imported-project.log section 1)

the CUDA template built with GAIN_DEFAULT=2.0 appends one line per render to $MCOFX_PATH_LOG with the stream it was given: eight renders, every one on the CUDA path, every one carrying a non-null kOfxImageEffectPropCudaStream (the same pointer for the session, at 1920x1080 and at a 288x162 thumbnail), and the rendered frame is the source times two to the byte (mae 0.0, max 0). Resolve supplies a stream; the property is not absent as the page assumed

the control for the host's 0xC0000409: a bundle with no CUDA provider and no cuDNN (OnnxInference.ofx + onnxruntime-ofx.dll only) loads, renders 1920x1080 and quits with exit 0; the label reports CPU (1 thread) - fallback: CUDA execution provider is not enabled in this build. The same log lists the four Resolve crash reports, in none of which a bundle of ours was loaded
